transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

The most likely causes are a blockage in the wand, floorhead or bin inlet, or a clogged/damp filter; less often it is the battery or its contacts. Check the filter too: wash it only in cold water if dirty, then leave it to dry fully for at least 24 hours before refitting—fitting it damp can cause the same pulsing.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal. no burning smell or heat or anything. what do i do first, ive not washed the filter ever tbh

First, wash the filter. On a V8, pulsing is usually the protection reacting to restricted airflow, and a filter that has never been washed is the leading suspect. 1. Switch it off and remove it from the charger. Take out the filter, rinse it under cold running water only—no detergent—and gently squeeze and tap out the dirt.
2. Leave it somewhere warm and ventilated for at least 24 hours, until completely dry. Do not refit it damp or use heat to dry it.
3. While it is drying, empty the bin and, with the machine off, remove the wand and floorhead. Look through the wand and inlet for compacted dust or hair; clear any blockage you can safely reach. Do not run it without the filter fitted. If it still pulses once the filter is clean and fully dry and the air path is clear, the next likely causes are a blockage deeper in the floorhead/bin inlet or, less commonly, the battery or its contacts.

washed the filter, water came out black lol. left it overnight on the radiator side. also found a big clump of hair and cat litter stuck at the bottom of the wand where the head goes on, pulled it out. its fine now, proper suction, no pulsin

That points to an airflow blockage rather than a battery fault: the hair and cat litter at the wand end were restricting the airflow, which makes a cordless Dyson pulse as protection. Keep the filter completely dry before refitting it; overnight by a radiator may be enough, but if it feels at all cool or damp, leave it longer in a ventilated room rather than directly on heat. Empty the bin regularly and check the wand/floorhead inlet when suction starts to drop. Is there anything else you need help with?
